actor_awards.notes: The preeminent leading man of Italian cinema during the 1960s and 70s, best known for his frequent collaborations with director Federico Fellini and his iconic pairing with Sophia Loren. He received Academy Award nominations for 'Divorce Italian Style', 'A Special Day', and 'Dark Eyes'.

filmography.title: 8½
filmography.role_description: A famous Italian film director suffering from a stifling creative block and retreating into his memories and fantasies.
filmography.plot: A harried movie director retreats into his memories and fantasies.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Win – Best Foreign Language Film, Best Costume Design (Black-and-White)

filmography.title: La Dolce Vita
filmography.role_description: A disillusioned, passive journalist who spends seven days and nights navigating the decadence of Rome's high society.
filmography.plot: A series of stories following a week in the life of a philandering paparazzo journalist living in Rome.
filmography.awards: Cannes Film Festival: Win – Palme d'Or

filmography.title: Divorce Italian Style (Divorzio all'italiana)
filmography.role_description: A bored Sicilian nobleman who concocts an elaborate scheme to murder his wife so he can marry his young cousin.
filmography.plot: A married Sicilian baron falls in love with his cousin and vows to wed her, but with divorce illegal he must concoct a crime of passion to dispose of his wife.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Actor; BAFTA: Win – Best Foreign Actor

filmography.title: A Special Day (Una giornata particolare)
filmography.role_description: A suicidal, anti-fascist gay radio announcer who forms a brief, profound connection with a conservative housewife (Sophia Loren) on the day Hitler visits Rome.
filmography.plot: Two neighbors, a persecuted journalist and a resigned housewife, meet during Hitler's visit to Italy in May 1938.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Actor; Golden Globe: Win – Best Foreign Film

filmography.title: La Notte (The Night)
filmography.role_description: A successful author who spends a long, alienated night traversing Milan's social scene as his marriage deteriorates.
filmography.plot: A day in the life of an unfaithful married couple and their steadily deteriorating relationship.
filmography.awards: Berlin International Film Festival: Win – Golden Bear

filmography.title: Dark Eyes (Oci ciornie)
filmography.role_description: An aging, charming Italian architect who recounts his tragic, unfulfilled romance with a Russian woman.
filmography.plot: An Italian man tells a fellow passenger on a cruise ship the story of his romance with a Russian woman.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Actor; Cannes Film Festival: Win – Best Actor

filmography.title: Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow (Ieri oggi domani)
filmography.role_description: Mastroianni plays three distinct roles—a working-class husband, a wealthy intellectual, and a naive client—opposite Sophia Loren in this anthology comedy.
filmography.plot: Stories about three very different women and the men they attract.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Win – Best Foreign Language Film; BAFTA: Win – Best Foreign Actor

filmography.title: Marriage Italian Style (Matrimonio all'italiana)
filmography.role_description: A wealthy Neapolitan businessman who refuses to marry his long-time mistress (Sophia Loren) until she tricks him.
filmography.plot: A cynical, successful businessman is tricked into marriage by his longtime mistress.
filmography.awards: Golden Globe: Win – Best Foreign-Language Foreign Film

filmography.title: The Tenth Victim (La decima vittima)
filmography.role_description: A participant in a futuristic, televised game of legalized murder who falls for his assigned killer (Ursula Andress).
filmography.plot: In the future, humans hunt each other for sport and entertainment. A man and a woman are assigned to kill each other, but they fall in love instead.

filmography.title: Big Deal on Madonna Street (I soliti ignoti)
filmography.role_description: A photographer raising his baby alone who joins a group of incompetent thieves planning a heist.
filmography.plot: A group of bungling thieves attempt to rob a pawnshop in Rome.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Foreign Language Film

filmography.title: City of Women (La città delle donne)
filmography.role_description: A man who gets off a train and wanders into a surreal, dreamlike world populated entirely by aggressive, assertive women.
filmography.plot: A businessman on a train has a brief encounter with a woman, follows her, and ends up in a bizarre hotel hosting a feminist convention.

filmography.title: Le Notti Bianche (White Nights)
filmography.role_description: A lonely newcomer to Livorno who falls in love with an emotional woman waiting for her lost lover.
filmography.plot: A lonely man meets a woman crying on a bridge and they spend several nights talking, but she is waiting for her lover to return.
filmography.awards: Venice Film Festival: Win – Silver Lion

filmography.title: A Fine Romance (Maccheroni)
filmography.role_description: An Italian man who has spent 40 years writing fake letters to his sister from an American soldier (Jack Lemmon) she briefly met.
filmography.plot: A stressed American executive returns to Naples and reunites with an old acquaintance who has been secretly living a lie on his behalf.

filmography.title: Ginger and Fred
filmography.role_description: An aging dancer who reunites with his former partner to perform their Fred Astaire/Ginger Rogers routine on a crass television variety show.
filmography.plot: Two aging dancers, who used to perform a Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers impersonation act, reunite after many years for a TV variety show.
filmography.awards: Golden Globe: Nomination – Best Foreign Language Film

filmography.title: Everybody's Fine (Stanno tutti bene)
filmography.role_description: An elderly Sicilian widower who travels across Italy to visit his five adult children, only to discover their lives are not as perfect as they claimed.
filmography.plot: An aging father visits his children in different cities, only to discover they have been lying to him about their success and happiness.
filmography.awards: Cannes Film Festival: Win – Prize of the Ecumenical Jury

filmography.title: La Grande Bouffe
filmography.role_description: An airline pilot who is one of four successful men who gather at a villa with the intention of eating themselves to death.
filmography.plot: Four successful middle-aged men gather at a villa to gorge themselves to death on fine food and sex.
filmography.awards: Cannes Film Festival: Win – FIPRESCI Prize

filmography.title: Sunflower (I Girasoli)
filmography.role_description: An Italian soldier missing in action on the Russian front during WWII, whose wife (Sophia Loren) travels to the Soviet Union to find him.
filmography.plot: An Italian woman searches for her husband, a soldier missing in Russia since WWII.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Original Score

filmography.title: Casanova 70
filmography.role_description: An Italian NATO officer who can only find romantic success in situations of extreme danger.
filmography.plot: A NATO officer seeks psychiatric help because he can only achieve sexual arousal when his life is in danger.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Original Screenplay

filmography.title: The Organizer (I compagni)
filmography.role_description: A charismatic intellectual who arrives in Turin to help organize textile workers in a strike.
filmography.plot: In late 19th-century Turin, textile workers face brutal conditions and go on strike, aided by an idealistic intellectual.
filmography.awards: Oscar: Nomination – Best Original Screenplay

filmography.title: Ready to Wear (Prêt-à-Porter)
filmography.role_description: A mysterious Italian returning to Paris during fashion week, hoping to reunite with an old flame (Sophia Loren).
filmography.plot: A sprawling ensemble comedy chronicling the chaos and interconnected lives of designers, reporters, and models during Paris Fashion Week.
filmography.awards: Golden Globe: Nomination – Best Motion Picture - Musical or Comedy

filmography.title: A Slightly Pregnant Man (L'Événement le plus important depuis que l'homme a marché sur la lune)
filmography.role_description: A Parisian driving instructor who inexplicably becomes pregnant, much to the shock of his fiancée (Catherine Deneuve) and the medical community.
filmography.plot: A driving instructor inexplicably becomes pregnant, causing a media sensation and challenging gender roles.

filmography.title: Family Diary (Cronaca familiare)
filmography.role_description: A journalist who reflects on his troubled relationship with his younger, dying brother.
filmography.plot: A journalist remembers his difficult relationship with his younger brother after receiving news of his death.
filmography.awards: Venice Film Festival: Win – Golden Lion

filmography.title: Leo the Last
filmography.role_description: An exiled European prince living in London who slowly becomes radicalized by the poverty around him.
filmography.plot: An exiled prince moves to a slum in London and gradually becomes involved with the local residents and their struggles.
filmography.awards: Cannes Film Festival: Win – Best Director (John Boorman)

filmography.title: Sostiene Pereira (According to Pereira)
filmography.role_description: An aging, apolitical journalist in 1930s fascist Portugal who is slowly drawn into the resistance.
filmography.plot: A complacent culture editor at a Lisbon newspaper during the Salazar dictatorship slowly awakens to the political reality around him.
filmography.awards: David di Donatello: Win – Best Actor
